_about: The maker's specification for a product, shown on the product page of a piece that is that product: a watch through piece.reference (its reference number), anything else through piece.spec (a key). Only for pieces identified exactly: the reference or product named in S&L's own caption, legible in S&L's photo, or recorded as confirmed in assets/SOURCES.md; nothing 'of this kind'. kind says whose wording it is: maker (the maker's own page), retailer (an official retailer's copy of the maker's catalogue; rolex.com refuses automated requests), dealer or press (second choice, where the maker's page refuses automated requests), law (the statute that defines a coin). It describes the product as made, not the condition, papers or packaging of S&L's piece. Researched 8 Oct 2026; every value was checked on its source page that day.

source.name: Raffi Jewellers, official Rolex retailer (M126333-0020)
source.note: The suffixes in the brief do not match what official retailers list. The slate 'Wimbledon' Jubilee is M126333-0020; its Dial row reads 'Slate'. The olive-green Jubilee is M126333-0024; its Dial row reads 'Olive green' (https://raffijewellers.com/rolex/datejust-41-m126333-0024/, also https://www.pragnell.co.uk/rolex/datejust-41-m126333-0024_126333). Every other row is word-for-word identical on both pages, so the rows above cover both, and Dial is left out because it differs. M126333-0022 is not listed by any official retailer I could read. Dealer sources (WatchMaxx https://www.watchmaxx.com/rolex-watch-m126333-0022, and WatchBase in search results) describe it as a champagne fluted-motif dial on a Jubilee bracelet, so it is neither green variant. Rolex's own wording for the slate dial is just 'Slate': the green Roman numerals and the 'Wimbledon' name are not in the maker's spec.

source.name: Raffi Jewellers, official Rolex retailer (M228349RBR-0036)
source.note: Covers M228349RBR-0036 only, because other 228349RBR suffixes have different dials. Retailer copy for the dial: 'This dial features 8 baguette-cut diamonds and 2 baguette-cut sapphires at 6 and 9 o'clock.' Kapoor Watch Co., also an official retailer (https://www.kapoorwatch.com/rolex/watches/rolex-day-date-m228349rbr-0036), gives the same rows, with the bezel worded 'Set with diamonds' and the certification as 'COSC + Rolex certification after casing'.

source.name: Goldsmiths, official Rolex retailer: Rolex Certified Pre-Owned listing (2000 example)
source.note: This is a discontinued reference, so the rows are the period specification from the Rolex Certified Pre-Owned spec table. That table appears verbatim on Mappin & Webb (https://www.mappinandwebb.com/Rolex-Certified-Pre+Owned-Cosmograph-Daytona-16520/p/40410625, 1999 example). The listing gives no water resistance or certification, so those rows are left out. Blowers Jewellers, an independent dealer (https://blowers-jewellers.co.uk/product/rolex-cosmograph-daytona-16520/), states 'water resistant up to 100 metres', a 'chronometer-certified calibre 4030' and 'an approximate 54-hour power reserve'. Power-reserve figures for the 4030 disagree: Blowers gives 54 h, the Rolex CPO listing gives 55 h (used above), and unverified search snippets gave other figures between 44 and 50 h. Sotheby's guide (https://www.sothebys.com/en/articles/the-rolex-daytona-zenith-a-sothebys-guide) confirms the 40 mm steel case, calibre 4030 (a modified Zenith El Primero) and production from 1988 to 2000. Dial colour varies by watch, so there is no Dial row.
